_README: WHAT THIS IS. A record of which recurring failure classes ALREADY have a general gate, so the
digest's recurring-class table can say so. Read by scripts/generate-known-failure-modes.py and
by nothing else. It changes no verdict and blocks no build: it adds one column to a page agents
read before acting.
WHY IT EXISTS (improvement review 2026-09-18-improvement-review-2, IMP-0763 + IMP-0764). The
recurring-class table is derived purely from how many times a class has occurred, so its heading
read 'where a general gate is missing' for every row — including rows whose gate exists, is
wired, and had just caught the very defect being logged. On 2026-09-18 two findings followed
that instruction and proposed building a general check into scripts/verify-pipeline-config.py,
whose checks 11 and 14 had each caught one of them minutes earlier. A read path that recommends
building what already exists costs a dispatch every time it is believed.
THE ONE RULE FOR ADDING A ROW. 'property' is the sub-property the gate ACTUALLY defends, never
the whole class name. A class name is a label several distinct mechanisms end up sharing:
config-placeholder-known-but-not-fixed covers both a placeholder in a deploymentSettings JSON
file (defended here) and a pending id in solution-source XML that only a live write can resolve
(not defended, and not defensible by a gate). Recording the class as defended would suppress a
gate the other half still needs.
AN ABSENT CLASS MEANS 'NO DEFENCE RECORDED', NEVER 'NO DEFENCE EXISTS'. The file is opt-in and
seeded with two entries against 56 recurring classes, so it under-claims by construction. That
asymmetry is deliberate and is the safe direction: under-claiming costs one grep that finds an
existing gate, while over-claiming would suppress a gate that genuinely needs building.
'proves_green' is a command, not a description. Anyone can run it to check the claim is still
true, which is the whole point — a defence recorded here and since deleted is worse than no
record at all.

defences.property: an unresolved {{TOKEN}} in a value position of provisioning/deploymentSettings/*.json with no matching entry in that file's own _unresolved block
defences.defended_by: scripts/verify-pipeline-config.py check 11 (check_settings_content) — walks every value position by dot-path, requires a matching _unresolved declaration carrying path/owner/why/expires, and fails on a missing, unowned OR EXPIRED one
defences.not_covered: a {PENDING-...} id in solution-source XML (IMP-0166, IMP-0243) — single braces, different files, and resolvable only by a live write, so no gate can clear it

defences.property: a blocked_on note in config/<slug>-pipeline.yml whose blocked_on_asserted date has passed the 14-day re-test limit
defences.defended_by: scripts/verify-pipeline-config.py check 14 (check_blocked_on_staleness, BLOCKED_ON_MAX_AGE_DAYS = 14) — HARD, with a 4-day pre-expiry WARNING (IMP-0585) and check_resolved_note_cleared for a note re-dated where it should have been removed (IMP-0602)
defences.not_covered: a deferral recorded somewhere other than a pipeline blocked_on note — an improvement-log entry left behind by a review is a DIFFERENT mechanism under the same class name, defended separately by verify-improvement-log.py check_left_behind (IMP-0762). Also not covered: automatically re-running a note's stated discharge condition, because those conditions are written as YAML COMMENTS and the gate parses the file with yaml.safe_load, which discards them (measured 0 of 5 notes exposing a machine-readable condition, 2026-09-18)

defences.property: an FR-/NFR-/US-/OQ- identifier declared by two documents under docs/plans/, AND a docs/plans/ document carrying no id-allocation declaration at all — read_declarations parses the `<!-- id-allocation: ... -->` comment, so an undeclared document is invisible to the collision check and is therefore failed in its own right rather than skipped
defences.defended_by: scripts/verify-requirement-id-uniqueness.py — HARD, build step 19. Its check covers BOTH halves: the undeclared-document half (NO ID DECLARATION, the finding message naming the exact comment to add, including the `none` form for a document that only cites ids allocated elsewhere) and the genuine-collision half (ID ALLOCATED TWICE, grouped by the clashing document pair)
defences.not_covered: THE A-nnn ASSUMPTION-REGISTER NAMESPACE, which is where this class's remaining live instances actually are. Unvalidated Assumptions Register ids (A-FIN-nn, A-FLOW-nn, A-DS-n, A-TRM-n) live in docs/development/*-dev-summary.md, are allocated per document, and NOTHING checks them for cross-document collision: verify-assumption-markers.py resolves an OPEN row to its source marker and verify-assumption-register.py checks a row's status against its own narrative, and neither compares ids BETWEEN documents. Measured 2026-09-18: 56 distinct A-nnn ids carrying register rows, 5 appearing in more than one document, of which 3 are true collisions (A-DS-1 = DocuSign connector apiId vs muted/quiet state treatments; A-FIN-03 = REV_FinanceOnly fieldsecurityprofileid vs the rev_roundfinance Decimal classid, i.e. IMP-0703 still live as a duplicate ROW after IMP-0707 fixed only the source MARKER; A-FLOW-13 = result() on Switch/If vs unscored-application exclusion, authored 2026-09-18) and 2 are legitimate carry-forwards of the same assumption into a successor document (A-TRM-1, A-TRM-2). A naive same-id-two-documents rule therefore measures 3 true of 5 — 60% — which is below the bar for wiring, so no gate is claimed here. Tracked as IMP-0768. Also not covered: a wbs: tag resolving to no accepted task (verify-wbs-chain.py, SUITE_GATE_EXEMPT, runs at PM gates not at build).
